gaps: NumTracingThreads is a runtime dispatch value from the tracing tile classification; it is not stored in this buffer's descriptor.

resourceSchemas.quantity: per-pixel temporal accumulation confidence of the reflection denoiser, stored as a normalized UNORM float
resourceSchemas.units: frame count in [0,32]; stored = count/32, decoded = code*32

storage.extent: View scene-texture extent (effective texture resolution), one slice per ResolvedClosureCount

mathTerms: Because the texture is UNORM8 and the pack divides by 32, the representable frame counts are quantized in steps of 32/255 ~= 0.125 frames.
Zero disables history (valid values are clamped to >= 0.004 elsewhere for LightIsMoving, but this texture has no such clamp).
gaps: FrontLayer.<Name> is an alias used for the translucent front layer (LumenReflections.cpp:1722); storage and decode are identical, only the effective extent differs (front layer uses the full scene extent without Substrate closure scaling).
MaxFramesAccumulated is a runtime CVar-derived value; counts above 32 saturate the UNORM encoding (decode can never exceed 32), and the quantization step is 32/255.

resourceSchemas.quantity: distance to trace each reflection ray before falling back to radiance-cache interpolation, plus a bool flag in bit 15
resourceSchemas.units: f16 distance (world units, cm) in bits[0:14]; bit15 = bUseRadianceCache
resourceSchemas.coordinateSpace: 2D screen-space array slice per closure; value is a ray parameter t

fields.name: RayTraceDistance
fields.decode: f16tof32(code & 0x7FFF); clamped to GetMaxHitDistance()=MaxHalfFloat at pack

mathTerms: Stored as R16_UINT (not R16F) because bit 15 carries the flag; the low 15 bits are an IEEE half bit pattern.
GetMaxHitDistance() = MaxHalfFloat = 65504, so the f16 clamp is lossless for legal trace distances.
gaps: The flag is a single bit; there is no room for a second boolean in this format.

resourceSchemas.quantity: list of 8x8 resolve tiles whose reflection output must be cleared (packed tile coordinate, optional closure index)
resourceSchemas.units: packed uint32 (12-bit x, 12-bit y, optional 3-bit closure)

storage.capacity: NumResolveTiles elements = ceil(extent/8).X*Y*TracedClosureCount; valid count = ClearTileIndirectArgs.x

mathTerms: PackTileCoord12bits = (x & 0xFFF) | ((y & 0xFFF) << 12) (PackUnpack.ush:402,409).
The list is appended with wave prefix sums, so entries are in classification order, not sorted.
gaps: Only [0, ClearTileIndirectArgs.x) is written; the rest of the NumResolveTiles capacity is uninitialized.
When an external SingleLayerWater tiled-reflection list is used, this buffer is replaced by the external SRV (LumenReflections.cpp:1343).

resourceSchemas.quantity: linear scene depth at each downsampled reflection tracing texel, signed to mark invalid rays
resourceSchemas.units: world-space linear depth (cm); negative = invalid/unlit probe; 0 = unused closure slice; -1 = cleared tile

fields.name: SceneDepth
fields.decode: value = Material.SceneDepth; if the ray is invalid the value is negated (value < 0 means invalid); cleared tiles store -1; unused closure slices store 0

transforms.name: invalid
transforms.expression: if (!bRayValid) DownsampledDepth = -abs(DownsampledDepth); world position reconstruction uses abs(depth)

mathTerms: SceneDepth is the same linear depth used by GetTranslatedWorldPositionFromScreenUV(ScreenUV, SceneDepth) (LumenPosition.ush:16-19), i.e. world-space Z in cm, not device Z.
The sign bit is the only invalidity channel; 0 is a legal depth only for unused closure slices (written at LumenReflections.usf:433).
gaps: The value is a depth of the traced receiver pixel, not the reflection hit distance; hit distance lives in TraceHit/ResolvedSpecularIndirectDepth.

resourceSchemas.quantity: per-texel reflection ray direction and cone angle (with first-person flag in the sign)
resourceSchemas.units: xyz = unit world-space direction; w = signed cone half-angle (radians); |w| in (0,PI/2]
resourceSchemas.coordinateSpace: world space direction; one array slice per closure

fields.name: SignedConeHalfAngle
fields.decode: w = -ConeHalfAngle for first-person pixels, +ConeHalfAngle otherwise; ConeHalfAngle = max(1/PDF, MinReflectionConeAngle)

transforms.name: encode
transforms.expression: w = bIsFirstPerson ? -ConeHalfAngle : ConeHalfAngle, with ConeHalfAngle = max(1/max(Sample.PDF,1e-4), MinReflectionConeAngle)

mathTerms: MinReflectionConeAngle = 0.00001 (LumenReflectionCommon.ush:119); PDF is clamped to >= 0.0001 at LumenReflections.usf:362/387 before inversion.
The 16-bit half storage quantizes both direction and cone angle; the direction is not renormalized after storage.
gaps: There is no separate PDF channel: PDF is recovered as 1/|w|, so a stored 0 (or denormal) would produce an infinite PDF; the encode clamps ConeHalfAngle >= 1e-5, which bounds PDF <= 1e5.

resourceSchemas.quantity: list of 8x8 resolve tiles that the reflection resolve/denoise passes must process
resourceSchemas.units: packed uint32 (12-bit x, 12-bit y, optional closure)
mathTerms: Uses the same PackTileData encoding as ReflectionClearTileData; only the producer/consumer tile set differs.
gaps: Valid count is ResolveTileIndirectArgs.x, not the NumResolveTiles capacity.

resourceSchemas.quantity: dispatch count for the reflection denoiser resolve/temporal/spatial passes
resourceSchemas.units: thread-group counts (x,y,z)

fields.name: X
fields.decode: record.x = number of resolve tiles appended

transforms.name: init
transforms.expression: x starts at 0 and is atomically incremented per accepted resolve tile; y=z=1

mathTerms: Temporal accumulation and spatial filtering both dispatch with this buffer at offset 0 (LumenReflections.cpp:1765,1815).
gaps: The same count is reused by several denoiser passes but those passes also read ReflectionResolveTileData to map tile index -> screen coord, so count and list must stay in sync.

resourceSchemas.quantity: resolved reflection radiance before temporal accumulation (denoiser input), per texel
resourceSchemas.units: linear pre-exposed radiance (RGB); sentinel INVALID_LIGHTING for cleared tiles
resourceSchemas.coordinateSpace: 2D screen-space array slice per resolved closure; effective texture resolution

fields.name: RadianceR
fields.decode: red of the resolved reflection radiance; sentinel 65024 for tiles cleared by the denoiser clear pass

transforms.name: write
transforms.expression: resolved radiance = DenoiserSpaceToRGB(weighted spatial average of RGBToDenoiserSpace(TraceRadiance))

mathTerms: INVALID_LIGHTING is deliberately the largest representable value family for R11G11B10 so it cannot collide with legal radiance.
The resolve converts to denoiser space for filtering and back to linear RGB before storing (LumenReflectionResolve.usf:632-649).
gaps: FrontLayer.<Name> is an alias for the translucent front layer; same format/decode, different extent (full scene extent for front layer).
The clear pass writes RGB only for tiles in ClearTileIndirectArgs; other tiles are covered by the resolve pass or remain uninitialized.

resourceSchemas.quantity: minimum ray hit distance of the resolved reflection samples (used by the reflection denoiser for disocclusion/neighborhood rejection)
resourceSchemas.units: world-space distance from the receiver along the ray (cm); large/Inf = no valid hit
resourceSchemas.coordinateSpace: 2D screen-space array slice per resolved closure

fields.name: MinRayHitT
fields.decode: minimum DecodeRayDistance() over accepted samples; FLOAT_32_MAX is written when no sample hit (R16F store saturates), so treat >=65504 or +Inf as 'no hit'

transforms.name: write
transforms.expression: value = Center.MinRayHitT = min over samples of abs(EncodeRayDistance(HitDistance,bHit)); initialized to FLOAT_32_MAX

mathTerms: The value is a positive distance; the hit/miss flag is not stored here (TraceHit carries it).
Because FLOAT_32_MAX (~3.4e38) exceeds the R16F maximum (65504), the stored 'no hit' value is a saturated/overflowed encoding rather than an exact sentinel.
gaps: The clear pass does not write this texture (LumenReflectionDenoiserClear.usf:32 writes RGB only), so texels outside the resolve tile set are uninitialized; consumers are dispatched over the same resolve tiles.

resourceSchemas.quantity: final denoised reflection specular radiance used by the reflection composite
resourceSchemas.units: linear pre-exposed radiance (RGB)
resourceSchemas.coordinateSpace: 2D screen-space array slice per resolved closure

fields.name: RadianceR
fields.decode: red of the spatially filtered reflection radiance

transforms.name: write
transforms.expression: value = DenoiserSpaceToRGB( specular lighting / weight sum ) after bilateral spatial filtering

mathTerms: Created with TexCreate_RenderTargetable in addition to SRV/UAV (LumenReflections.cpp:1779) because some composite paths render into it.
gaps: Declared with FClearValueBinding::Transparent (0) and there is no INVALID_LIGHTING sentinel here, so a cleared/unwritten texel is indistinguishable from a true black reflection.

resourceSchemas.quantity: signed ray hit distance of the reflection trace (negative = hit, positive = miss)
resourceSchemas.units: distance in cm; |value| = hit distance, sign = hit flag
resourceSchemas.coordinateSpace: 2D screen-space array slice per traced closure

fields.name: EncodedDistance
fields.decode: value = HitDistance * (bHit ? -1 : +1); decode: bHit = signbit(value) (asuint(value)&0x8000 for the 16-bit pattern); HitDistance = abs(value)

transforms.name: decode
transforms.expression: bHit = asuint(Encoded) & 0x80000000 (f32 path) / sign bit of the half; HitDistance = abs(Encoded)

mathTerms: Misses store the max trace distance with a positive sign; there is no separate miss sentinel besides the sign.
The R16F store quantizes hit distance; very large miss distances clamp to MaxHalfFloat=65504.
gaps: The hardware-ray-tracing path writes the same encoding (LumenReflectionHardwareRayTracing.usf:395), so the decode is path-independent.

resourceSchemas.quantity: radiance returned by the reflection ray at the hit point (or miss/sky value)
resourceSchemas.units: linear pre-exposed radiance (multiply by 1/View.PreExposure for physical radiance)
resourceSchemas.coordinateSpace: 2D screen-space array slice per traced closure

transforms.name: store
transforms.expression: TraceRadiance = TraceResult.Lighting * View.PreExposure (radiance-cache-sourced samples are already de-preexposed by the cache; the final product is pre-exposed)

transforms.name: hardwarePath
transforms.expression: same store: MakeFinite(TraceResult.Lighting) after the HW RT payload, which is already pre-exposed at trace time

mathTerms: Software and hardware tracing both write pre-exposed radiance; the composite divides by View.PreExposure via the scene-color pipeline.
MakeFinite() is applied only in the HW path; the SW path relies on the trace result being finite.
gaps: The 29-bit float-packing used by screen-probe TraceHit does not apply here: reflection TraceHit is a plain R16F with sign-as-hit.

resourceSchemas.quantity: dispatch count for FReflectionGenerateRaysCS over downsampled tracing tiles
resourceSchemas.units: thread-group counts (x,y,z)

transforms.name: init
transforms.expression: x starts at 0, y=z=1; GenerateRays dispatches with this buffer at offset 0

mathTerms: TracingTileViewportMin/Dimensions use TracingTileSize = ReflectionDownsampleFactorXY * 8 (LumenReflections.cpp:803-806).
gaps: This is also the source of NumTracingThreads for CompactionIndirectArgs (the compaction setup reads this buffer as an SRV).

resourceSchemas.quantity: per uniform screen-probe bitmask of the sample positions that need an adaptive probe spawned
resourceSchemas.units: bit i = 1 if sample i (of NumSamplesPerUniformProbe) requires an adaptive probe; bits >= NumSamplesPerUniformProbe are 0
resourceSchemas.coordinateSpace: screen-tile grid = ceil(SceneTextures extent / ScreenProbeDownsampleFactor); one texel per uniform probe

fields.name: SampleMask
fields.decode: bit i = needs probe; i = SampleIndex2D.x + NumSamplesPerUniformProbe2D.x*SampleIndex2D.y; sample is marked when interpolation coverage dot(Weights,1) < MIN_PROBE_INTERPOLATION_WEIGHT

transforms.name: mark
transforms.expression: SampleMask = 1 << SampleIndex; InterlockedOr into the group-shared mask, then sample 0 writes the texel

mathTerms: MIN_PROBE_INTERPOLATION_WEIGHT = 0.01 (LumenScreenProbeGather.usf:36); NumSamplesPerUniformProbe is 4, 8 or 16 depending on the CVar r.Lumen.ScreenProbeGather.NumAdaptiveProbes clamped to [0,64] (LumenScreenProbeGather.cpp:2335).
Bits are written only when the adaptive-probe path is enabled; otherwise the texture is not created at all.
gaps: The effective sample count is a permutation constant (FNumSamplesPerUniformProbe); the number of meaningful bits cannot be recovered from the texel alone.

resourceSchemas.quantity: screen-space positions of the adaptive probes spawned this frame, indexed after the uniform probes
resourceSchemas.units: packed uint32: low 16 bits = screen x, high 16 bits = screen y (pixel coordinates, viewport-relative offset included)

storage.capacity: max(MaxNumAdaptiveProbes,1) elements; valid count = min(NumAdaptiveScreenProbes[0], MaxNumAdaptiveProbes)

mathTerms: Probes are spawned only while AdaptiveProbeIndex < MaxNumAdaptiveProbes; the counter NumAdaptiveScreenProbes[0] may exceed the capacity and is clamped by consumers.
gaps: The buffer is cleared to 0 when adaptive probes are disabled; that 0 is indistinguishable from a valid probe at screen (0,0) but the consumer clamps by NumAdaptiveScreenProbes[0]=0.

resourceSchemas.quantity: spherical-harmonic representation of the aggregated BRDF probability density over each probe's interpolation footprint
resourceSchemas.units: 9 SH coefficients (unitless density coefficients) per probe; stored as 16-bit floats
resourceSchemas.coordinateSpace: per-probe SH basis: [V0.x, V0.y, V0.z, V0.w, V1.x, V1.y, V1.z, V1.w, V2.x]

storage.capacity: ScreenProbeAtlasBufferSize.X*Y*NUM_PDF_SH_COEFFICIENTS(9) elements; valid count = same (every probe writes 9 coefficients)

fields.name: SHCoefficient0
fields.decode: element[probe*9 + 0] = average of CalcDiffuseTransferSH3(worldNormal).V0.x over accepted footprint pixels

fields.name: SHCoefficient1to7
fields.decode: elements[probe*9 + 1..7] = V0.y, V0.z, V0.w, V1.x, V1.y, V1.z, V1.w

transforms.name: writeIndex
transforms.expression: WriteIndex = (AtlasCoord.y*ScreenProbeAtlasViewSize.x + AtlasCoord.x) * 9 + ThreadIndex; value = SharedSphericalHarmonic[0][ThreadIndex] / SharedNumElements

transforms.name: read
transforms.expression: SHBaseIndex = probeIndex * NUM_PDF_SH_COEFFICIENTS; V0 = [c0,c1,c2,c3], V1 = [c4..c7], V2.x = c8

mathTerms: The buffer is declared Buffer<float> in HLSL but created with PF_R16F (2 B/element), so values are half-precision (LumenScreenProbeImportanceSamplingShared.ush:6; LumenScreenProbeImportanceSampling.cpp:283).
The SH is the average cosine-lobe transfer of the surface normals in the probe footprint, not the final light PDF; it is combined with the lighting PDF at sampling time.
gaps: If SharedNumElements is 0 the division is by 0 and no write occurs (guarded by the bAnySampleValid path); those probes keep uninitialized/stale coefficients.
The quantity is a normalized SH distribution, not radiance: its integral over the sphere is 1 for a valid probe.

resourceSchemas.quantity: backface diffuse indirect lighting computed by the screen-probe integrate pass (two-sided foliage/backface shading)
resourceSchemas.units: pre-exposed radiance (same space as ScreenProbeRadiance); multiplied by material diffuse color in the composite, not divided by PI again

fields.name: LightingR
fields.decode: red of the accumulated backface diffuse radiance

transforms.name: accumulate
transforms.expression: BackfaceDiffuseLighting += InterpolatedRadiance * BackfaceLightingSampleWeight (or PreintegratedTwoSidedBxDF * BackfaceSHDiffuseLighting); written quantized by BlueNoiseScalar

mathTerms: Only written when SUPPORT_BACKFACE_DIFFUSE is 1 (compile-time; requires the two-sided/backface diffuse permutation).
Unlike RWDiffuseIndirect, no Diffuse_Lambert(1/PI) factor is applied at store (compare LumenScreenProbeGather.usf:1459 and :1499).
gaps: The RDG buffer is only allocated when the integrate pass supports backface diffuse; its absence is a permutation, not an inactive family.
Values are dithered before the R11G11B10 store, so a single texel is not an exact deterministic function of the lighting.

resourceSchemas.quantity: list of integrate tiles that are not integrated this frame but still contain stale radiance and must be cleared
resourceSchemas.units: packed uint32 (12-bit tile x, 12-bit tile y, optional 3-bit closure)
resourceSchemas.coordinateSpace: integrate-tile grid relative to the viewport

transforms.name: pack
transforms.expression: value = PackTileCoord12bits(Coord) | ((ClosureIndex & 0x7) << 24 when Substrate closure format)

mathTerms: Capacity excludes the per-mode factor of the IntegrateTileData buffer: ClearUnusedIntegrateTileData has (Closure0 + Closure1N) elements while IntegrateTileData has 3x that (one list per classification mode).
gaps: Only [0, ClearUnusedIntegrateTileIndirectArgs.x) is written; the tail is uninitialized.
The list is produced by the tile-classification pass and only exists when tile classification is enabled.

resourceSchemas.quantity: dispatch count for the pass that clears stale integrate tiles
resourceSchemas.units: thread-group counts (x,y,z)

transforms.name: init
transforms.expression: WriteDispatchIndirectArgs(buffer,0,0,1,1); the classification pass atomically appends one per stale tile

mathTerms: Cleared at the start of InitScreenProbeTileIndirectArgsCS (record 0 only).
gaps: A zero x produces a zero-group dispatch, which is legal; no sentinel is used.

resourceSchemas.quantity: four dispatch records for the screen-probe compacted-tracing post passes (64/32-thread variants for the main and light-sample lists)
resourceSchemas.units: thread-group counts (x,y,z)
resourceSchemas.coordinateSpace: flat compacted trace index / group size
mathTerms: Records 2/3 use allocator element [1] (the 'LightSample' compaction list), while the C++ allocation is one uint (LumenScreenProbeTracing.cpp:614).
gaps: Records 2 and 3 are computed from CompactedTraceTexelAllocator[1], but the allocator buffer is created with a single element and no shader in the scoped sources writes index 1. Their group counts therefore read out of the declared buffer (undefined/zero in practice) and cannot be source-decoded. Records 0/1 are exact.

resourceSchemas.quantity: count of compacted screen-probe trace texels written into CompactedTraceTexelData
resourceSchemas.units: trace-texel count (uint32); element [1] is read but never written in this source

fields.name: NumTraceTexels
fields.decode: element[0] = number of compacted traces (InterlockedAdd appends); element[1] is read by the indirect-args setup but has no writer

transforms.name: count
transforms.expression: element[0] accumulates SharedGroupSum / SharedTraceTexelAllocator per workgroup

mathTerms: Cleared to 0 before compaction (AddClearUAVPass at LumenScreenProbeTracing.cpp:617).
gaps: The buffer is created with 1 uint, yet SetupCompactedTracesIndirectArgsCS reads CompactedTraceTexelAllocator[1] for records 2/3. The intended two-list (main + light-sample) design is not realized in the scoped C++ allocation; reading index 1 is outside the declared buffer.

resourceSchemas.quantity: compact list of screen-probe trace texels (probe index + tracing texel coordinate)
resourceSchemas.units: packed uint32: 20-bit probe index, 5-bit x, 5-bit y
resourceSchemas.coordinateSpace: screen-probe atlas index and tracing-octahedron texel coordinate
mathTerms: 5-bit texel coordinates bound the tracing octahedron edge to 32 texels; the source supports up to 32x32 tracing resolution for this encoding.
gaps: Only [0, CompactedTraceTexelAllocator[0]) is written; the buffer capacity is the full tracing-buffer texel count.

resourceSchemas.quantity: one dispatch record per integrate tile-classification mode (SimpleDiffuse, SupportImportanceSampleBRDF, SupportAll), optionally doubled for Substrate overflow tiles
resourceSchemas.units: thread-group counts (x,y,z)

storage.capacity: ClassificationScaleFactor * 3 records (3 when Substrate is disabled, 6 when enabled)

transforms.name: init
transforms.expression: all records initialized to (0,1,1); the classification shader atomically increments x per accepted tile

mathTerms: Record order matches EScreenProbeIntegrateTileClassification { SimpleDiffuse, SupportImportanceSampleBRDF, SupportAll, Num } (LumenScreenProbeGather.h:90-96).
ClassificationScaleFactor = Substrate::IsSubstrateEnabled() ? 2 : 1 (LumenScreenProbeGather.cpp:1481); the captured descriptor has 3 records, i.e. Substrate disabled in this capture.
gaps: Read each record's y/z as 1, not 0: init writes (0,1,1) and only x is incremented.
Only the records for enabled classification modes are dispatched; the others may remain (0,1,1).

resourceSchemas.quantity: per-mode lists of 8x8 integrate tiles that need screen-probe integration
resourceSchemas.units: packed uint32 (12-bit tile x, 12-bit tile y, optional 3-bit closure)
resourceSchemas.coordinateSpace: integrate-tile grid relative to the viewport; list offset per classification mode and closure

storage.capacity: 3 * ((tileX*tileY) + tileX*tileY*(MaxClosurePerPixel-1)) elements; valid counts are the three IntegrateIndirectArgs.x values

transforms.name: listOffset
transforms.expression: Closure 0 lists at mode*(tileX*tileY); closure 1..N lists at mode*(tileX*tileY*MaxClosurePerPixel) + closure0 offset

transforms.name: unpack
transforms.expression: Coord = uint2(value & 0xFFF, (value>>12)&0xFFF); ClosureIndex as above; screen rect = (Coord+1)*INTEGRATE_TILE_SIZE / View.ViewResolutionFraction

mathTerms: Tile size GScreenProbeIntegrateTileSize is 8 (see INTEGRATE_TILE_SIZE use at LumenScreenProbeGather.usf:1620).
The offset formula is conservative (per-mode and per-closure reservations) rather than a single packed list.
gaps: Capacity is a worst-case reservation; only the first IntegrateIndirectArgs.x entries of the active mode are valid, and the non-active mode regions are uninitialized.
The Substrate closure bits are a compile-time permutation; with Substrate disabled the high byte is never written.

resourceSchemas.quantity: per-probe discrete probability density of incoming lighting over the tracing octahedron texels (used to importance-sample lighting)
resourceSchemas.units: normalized probability per texel (sum over one probe's texels ~= 1); stored as R16F
resourceSchemas.coordinateSpace: per-probe ScreenProbeTracingOctahedronResolution x ScreenProbeTracingOctahedronResolution equi-area octahedral/equi-area grid

fields.name: PDF
fields.decode: value = PDF / max(PDFSum,0.0001) where PDFSum is the per-probe reduction of the raw radiance PDF; consumers multiply by MipSize^2 when sampling a mip

transforms.name: normalize
transforms.expression: PDF_texel = rawPDF_texel / max(sum(rawPDF over probe texels), 0.0001)

mathTerms: The stored value is a probability (not radiance); the radiance itself remains in ScreenProbeRadiance and is sampled by the generated rays.
Only created when r.Lumen.ScreenProbeGather.ImportanceSampleIncomingLighting is enabled (LumenScreenProbeImportanceSampling.cpp:361).
gaps: Texture extent depends on the tracing octahedron resolution, which is a runtime CVar; the captured 640x672 confirms resolution 8 for the atlas buffer 80x84 in this frame.

resourceSchemas.quantity: number of adaptive probes spawned this frame (unclamped atomic counter)
resourceSchemas.units: probe count (uint32)

fields.name: Count
fields.decode: value = number of adaptive probes appended; consumers clamp to MaxNumAdaptiveProbes

mathTerms: The counter is incremented per workgroup with InterlockedAdd even for probes that are then rejected by the AdaptiveProbeIndex < MaxNumAdaptiveProbes test, so it can exceed both the buffer capacity and the spawned count.
gaps: Because rejected probes still increment the counter, Count is an upper bound, not the number of valid entries; use the clamp and the per-entry validity path.

resourceSchemas.quantity: rough-specular indirect lighting computed from screen probes (4 GGX-ish samples + diffuse lerp) for surfaces whose roughness is too high for reflection tracing
resourceSchemas.units: pre-exposed specular radiance (linear RGB)

fields.name: SpecularR
fields.decode: red of the rough specular radiance

transforms.name: choose
transforms.expression: SpecularLighting = RoughSpecularLighting when ROUGH_SPECULAR_ALONG_REFLECTION_DIRECTION, else DiffuseLighting/PI; lerped with DiffuseLerp

mathTerms: Only computed when INTEGRATE_TILE_CLASSIFICATION_MODE != TILE_CLASSIFICATION_SIMPLE_DIFFUSE; in SimpleDiffuse mode the texture is cleared to 0 (LumenScreenProbeGather.usf:1576).
Roughness is clamped to >= 0.2 before the rough-specular loop (LumenScreenProbeGather.usf:1521).
gaps: The buffer is shared/reused (CreateSharedRT) across frames in FrameTemporaries; only the current frame's tiles are valid.

resourceSchemas.quantity: binary per-probe disocclusion flag used by the spatial denoiser to reject history
resourceSchemas.units: 0 or 1 (R8 UNORM)

fields.name: ProbeDisoccluded
fields.decode: value = 1 when the accumulated disocclusion-pixel count >= SharedNumElements * SpatialFilterDisocclusionFraction, else 0

transforms.name: write
transforms.expression: SharedNumDisocclusionPixels is accumulated from per-sample bDisocclusionPixel; SharedNumElements counts accepted footprint pixels; the single texel stores the >= fraction comparison as 1.0 or 0.0

mathTerms: Only allocated when LumenScreenProbeGather::UseDisocclusionSpatialFilter() is true (LumenScreenProbeImportanceSampling.cpp:286-292).
gaps: The shader stores the comparison result as a float 0/1 into R8; there is no fractional disocclusion confidence.

resourceSchemas.quantity: spatially filtered screen-probe radiance (ping-pong target of the probe spatial filter passes)
resourceSchemas.units: pre-exposed radiance (linear RGB), same space as ScreenProbeRadiance

fields.name: RadianceR
fields.decode: red of the filtered probe radiance

transforms.name: filter
transforms.expression: for each gather texel: sum over tracing texels of TraceRadiance * SampleWeight * spatial weights / weight sum; SampleWeight = (GatherRes/MipSize)^2 and MaxRayIntensity is applied after the weight

mathTerms: The same RDG name is created once per spatial-filter pass in a ping-pong loop (GLumenScreenProbeSpatialFilterNumPasses, LumenScreenProbeFiltering.cpp:585-620), so the captured frame can contain many resources with this name; all have identical format/meaning.
Values are dithered with QuantizeForFloatRenderTarget using the frame index.
gaps: This is radiance (not irradiance): the final irradiance conversion is done later by ScreenProbeConvertToIrradianceCS or by the SH path.

resourceSchemas.quantity: probe radiance with a 1-texel border and mip chain, used for mip-filtered probe interpolation
resourceSchemas.units: pre-exposed radiance (linear RGB)
resourceSchemas.coordinateSpace: per-probe (GatherOctahedronResolution+2) equi-area grid with border, mip chain

fields.name: RadianceR
fields.decode: red; border texels are copies via OctahedralMapWrapBorder, mip>0 generated by FScreenProbeGenerateMipLevelCS

transforms.name: border
transforms.expression: ProbeTexelCoord = DispatchThreadId.xy / WithBorderRes; border texel = OctahedralMapWrapBorder(coord, WithBorderRes, 1)

transforms.name: mips
transforms.expression: for MipLevel 1..GLumenScreenProbeGatherNumMips-1, generate from the previous mip

mathTerms: ScreenProbeGatherOctahedronResolutionWithBorder = ScreenProbeGatherOctahedronResolution + 2 (the +1 texel border on each side).
The mip count is the CVar r.Lumen.ScreenProbeGather.NumMips; the captured descriptor has 1 mip, so only mip 0 is present in this frame.
gaps: If NumMips == 1 the mip generation loop does not run and mips field is exactly 1; do not assume a full chain from the name.

resourceSchemas.quantity: closest hit distance among the tracing samples that contributed to each gather texel (filtering input)
resourceSchemas.units: non-linear sqrt-encoded distance in R8 UNORM; decode to distance in cm

fields.name: EncodedHitDistance
fields.decode: code/255 = E = sqrt(d/GetProbeMaxHitDistance())*254/255 + 1/255; the source consumer decodes L = E*E*MaxHalfFloat, d_src = (L - 1/255)*255/254 (not the exact inverse of the encoder)

mathTerms: MaxHalfFloat = 65504 is GetProbeMaxHitDistance(); the sqrt encoding spends more precision near small distances.
The encoding is not the raw distance and not a linear UNORM; a linear read of the byte is wrong.

The source encode/decode pair is not algebraically inverse: encode adds 1/255 before squaring, decode subtracts it after multiplying by MaxHalfFloat. The consumer formula is recorded exactly as written, not re-derived.
gaps: When no tracing sample was valid, MinHitDistance is set to -1 (LumenScreenProbeFiltering.usf:148) and EncodeProbeHitDistanceForFiltering(-1) takes sqrt of a negative number; the resulting NaN converted to UNORM8 has no defined value. Treat such texels as invalid via ScreenProbeTraceMoving/coverage rather than decoding a sentinel from this byte.
Additionally, the encoder and the source decoder are not exact inverses (bias applied before vs after the square), so d_src carries a systematic bias whose size depends on the code.

resourceSchemas.quantity: six dispatch records used by the screen-probe passes: group-per-probe, thread-per-probe, trace compaction, thread-per-trace, thread-per-gather, thread-per-gather-with-border
resourceSchemas.units: thread-group counts (x,y,z)
resourceSchemas.coordinateSpace: screen-probe atlas grid in probes and octahedron texels

fields.name: GroupPerProbe
fields.decode: x = AtlasSizeInProbes.x; y = AtlasSizeInProbes.y; z=1 (one 8x8 group per probe)

transforms.name: setup
transforms.expression: AtlasSizeInProbes = uint2(ScreenProbeAtlasViewSize.x, ceil(GetNumScreenProbes()/ScreenProbeAtlasViewSize.x)); WriteArgs2D(index, GroupSize, AtlasSizeInProbes * Resolution)

mathTerms: PROBE_THREADGROUP_SIZE_2D = 8 is the group edge for records 0/1/3/4/5; record 2 (compaction) uses group size 16 (LumenScreenProbeGather.usf:328).
Each WriteArgs2D(Index, GroupSize, ThreadCount) writes (ceil(ThreadCount.x/GroupSize), ceil(ThreadCount.y/GroupSize), 1).
gaps: The atlas view size includes the adaptive-probe reserve rows (LumenScreenProbeGather.cpp:2225-2229), so the dispatch can cover unspawned probe slots; GetNumScreenProbes() clamps actual work.

resourceSchemas.quantity: per-probe fraction of gather texels whose traced lighting was classified as moving (temporal history confidence)
resourceSchemas.units: fraction in [0,1] stored as R8 UNORM

fields.name: MovingFraction
fields.decode: value = (sum of per-gather-texel moving weights)/(GatherRes^2); consumed as a history alpha, with 0 disabling history

mathTerms: Written by ScreenProbeCalculateMovingCS into the probe-atlas texel (no octahedron dilation).
The consumer uses it as a stochastic interpolation weight (LumenScreenProbeGather.usf:1450-1455) and clamps the encoded history alpha to >= 0.004.
gaps: The average is over all gather texels, including texels that had no valid sample and were written as 0 by the composite, so a partially covered probe reads a diluted moving fraction.

resourceSchemas.quantity: per-gather-texel accumulated screen-probe trace radiance (composited from tracing texels, before spatial filtering)
resourceSchemas.units: pre-exposed radiance (linear RGB); resampled with SampleWeight = (GatherRes/MipSize)^2 and clamped to MaxRayIntensity

fields.name: RadianceR
fields.decode: red of the composited trace radiance

transforms.name: composite
transforms.expression: sum over contributing tracing texels of TraceRadiance*SampleWeight, clamped to MaxRayIntensity; SampleWeight = (GatherRes/MipSize)^2

mathTerms: The radiance stored by the tracer is multiplied by View.PreExposure (LumenScreenProbeTracing.usf:663), so this atlas is pre-exposed.
An upsampled gather resolution is not supported and is visually marked with (0,0,10) at LumenScreenProbeFiltering.usf:110-114.
gaps: Texels that received no valid tracing sample are written as 0, but they are still interpolated unless coverage/moving weights exclude them.

resourceSchemas.quantity: per-probe ambient (L0) spherical-harmonic coefficient of the probe radiance, used by the SH3 irradiance path
resourceSchemas.units: linear radiance (the SH V0.x coefficient per RGB channel)
resourceSchemas.coordinateSpace: one texel per screen probe in the probe atlas; SH basis L0

fields.name: AmbientR
fields.decode: red L0 coefficient = RadianceSH.R.V0.x after the PI/res^2 normalization

mathTerms: Only created when the irradiance format is SH3 (EScreenProbeIrradianceFormat::SH3, LumenScreenProbeFiltering.cpp:640); otherwise ScreenProbeIrradianceWithBorder is created instead.
The shader writes float3 AmbientRGB into an R11G11B10 texture; there is no alpha channel to decode.
gaps: The stored coefficient is radiance, not irradiance; the cosine convolution (CalcDiffuseTransferSH3) is applied by the consumer.

resourceSchemas.quantity: per-probe directional (L1) SH coefficients of the probe radiance, luminance-normalized to 6 half4 texels per probe
resourceSchemas.units: optionally quantized directional SH coefficients; when SH_QUANTIZE_DIRECTIONAL_COEFFICIENTS each texel is code = coef/ambient*0.5+0.5
resourceSchemas.coordinateSpace: 6 texels per probe: 2 texels x 3 channels, X-strided by ScreenProbeAtlasViewSize.x

fields.name: RedCoefficients0
fields.decode: texel at x+0*AtlasViewSize: (V0.y, V0.z, V0.w, V1.x) for red

fields.name: RedCoefficients1
fields.decode: texel at x+1*AtlasViewSize: (V1.y, V1.z, V1.w, V2.x) for red

transforms.name: packQuantized
transforms.expression: Code = coef * (0.282095/basisScale) / max(AmbientChannel,1e-5) * 0.5 + 0.5, with basisScale 0.488603 for L1 and 1.092548/0.315392/0.546274 for L2 terms

mathTerms: The quantization is a compile-time permutation (SH_QUANTIZE_DIRECTIONAL_COEFFICIENTS); without it the texels hold raw half coefficients and the (2*code-1) decode must NOT be applied.
Six texels per probe is a channel-major layout: Red 0/1, Green 0/1, Blue 0/1, each offset by ScreenProbeAtlasViewSize.x.
The six fields above all start at byte 0 of their own texel; they are not overlapping fields of a single texel. Texel (x + k*AtlasViewSize.x, y) holds channel/coefficient pair k.
gaps: Whether the stored half values are quantized codes in [0,1] or raw coefficients is decided by the SH_QUANTIZE_DIRECTIONAL_COEFFICIENTS compilation define, which is not present in the captured metadata; the two decodes give different results and neither can be selected from the texel bytes alone.
The alpha channel of each half4 is unused (the 4th component is the next coefficient, not alpha).

resourceSchemas.quantity: per-gather-texel fraction of contributing tracing samples flagged as moving (input to ScreenProbeMoving)
resourceSchemas.units: fraction in [0,1] as R8 UNORM

fields.name: TexelMoving
fields.decode: value = sum(bMoving ? SampleWeight*WeightQuantizeScale : 0) * InvWeightQuantizeScale, i.e. the moving sample weight fraction

mathTerms: Written by FScreenProbeCompositeTracesWithScatterCS; the per-ray bMoving flag comes from DecodeProbeRayDistance(TraceHit).bMoving (LumenScreenProbeFiltering.usf:126-129).
gaps: This is an intermediate: ScreenProbeMoving is the probe-level average of the same quantity.

resourceSchemas.quantity: per-probe translated-world position reconstructed from scene depth and velocity
resourceSchemas.units: xyz in translated world units (cm); w = 0 (written, unused)
mathTerms: Full float32 is used because the position feeds temporal reprojection/history comparisons across frames.
This is translated world (view-translation-relative), not absolute world, and not the previous-frame position.
gaps: Probes whose scene depth is invalid still get a written position (the depth sign marks invalidity in ScreenProbeSceneDepth, not here); consumers must pair it with the depth texture.

resourceSchemas.quantity: per-probe screen-space motion speed (|world position - reprojected previous world position|) with two material flags packed into a half
resourceSchemas.units: 16-bit half bit pattern: bits[1:14] = speed in cm/frame; bit15 = bTwoSidedFoliage; bit0 = bHair
resourceSchemas.coordinateSpace: translated world displacement per frame (cm); indexed by probe atlas texel

fields.name: Speed
fields.decode: f16tof32(code & 0x7FFE); |current translated world position - previous translated world position|

transforms.name: decode
transforms.expression: speed = f16tof32(code & 0x7FFE); flags from bits 15 and 0

mathTerms: The speed is a per-frame displacement, so it is resolution-independent but frame-rate dependent; do not interpret it as cm/s without the frame delta.
The sign bit of the half is reused for bTwoSidedFoliage; the speed itself is non-negative by construction (length of a vector).
gaps: f32tof16 of a large displacement saturates at 65504; bits 14 and 15 of the exponent are shared with the flag encoding, so only the low 14 bits of the half pattern hold the magnitude.

resourceSchemas.quantity: per-screen-tile count of adaptive probes whose list entry lives in that tile
resourceSchemas.units: adaptive probe count (uint32) per screen tile

fields.name: Count
fields.decode: value = number of InterlockedAdd increments for this ScreenTileCoord (one per spawned adaptive probe), used as the list length

transforms.name: listIndex
transforms.expression: AdaptiveProbeCoord = (TileProbeIndex % DownsampleFactor, TileProbeIndex / DownsampleFactor) * ScreenProbeViewSize + ScreenTileCoord

mathTerms: The header is cleared to 0 with AddClearUAVPass before spawning; TexCreate_AtomicCompatible is required for the interlocked add.
The tile coordinate is GetScreenTileCoord(AdaptiveSampleScreenCoord), i.e. jitter-removed, viewport-relative.
gaps: The count indexes a fixed downsampleFactor x downsampleFactor slot grid per tile; if more probes than downsampleFactor^2 are spawned for one tile, TileProbeIndex exceeds the slot range but the header still increments (the index formula then aliases). This is bounded by construction only when the tile's probe samples are unique.

resourceSchemas.quantity: per-screen-tile list of adaptive probe indices, laid out in a downsampleFactor x downsampleFactor slot grid
resourceSchemas.units: adaptive probe index (uint16); 0 also occurs for cleared slots
resourceSchemas.coordinateSpace: screen-tile grid expanded by ScreenProbeDownsampleFactor (captured 1280x896 = 80*16 x 56*16)

transforms.name: address
transforms.expression: AdaptiveProbeCoord = (listIndex % DownsampleFactor, listIndex / DownsampleFactor) * ScreenProbeViewSize + ScreenTileCoord

mathTerms: The address formula is unusual: the slot grid is strided by ScreenProbeViewSize (probe-atlas tile size), not contiguous within a tile, because the texture covers the full downsampled screen.
The list is only valid up to the per-tile header count.
gaps: The texture is cleared to 0 when adaptive probes are disabled (LumenScreenProbeGather.cpp:2410), so 0 is both a valid probe index and the cleared value; use the header count to bound the list.

resourceSchemas.quantity: short-range ambient occlusion / bent normal used during screen-probe integration (format depends on r.Lumen.ShortRangeAO.BentNormal)
resourceSchemas.units: either packed bent normal (RGB111110) or scalar AO in [0,1], depending on the CVar and pass permutation
resourceSchemas.coordinateSpace: 2D screen-space array slice per closure; downsampled screen resolution

fields.name: BentNormalRGB111110
fields.decode: when OUTPUT_BENT_NORMAL: PackRGB111110(BentNormal*0.5+0.5); decode UnpackRGB111110(code)*2-1 -> unit bent normal

fields.name: AmbientOcclusion
fields.decode: when !OUTPUT_BENT_NORMAL: AmbientOcclusion/NumRays in [0,1] stored as R8

mathTerms: Both paths write the same RDG name; the format is selected at pass setup, so the descriptor format is the only discriminator.
The bent-normal path packs into R11G11B10 bits inside a uint (PackRGB111110), the AO path uses an 8-bit UNORM.
gaps: When the texture is PF_R8, decoding it as a packed bent normal is wrong (and vice versa). The captured 1280x888 PF_R32_UINT descriptor shows the bent-normal path for this runtime.
The AO value is averaged over NumRays; the ray count is not stored, so the confidence/precision of the scalar is not recoverable.

resourceSchemas.quantity: spatially filtered translucency-volume trace radiance (output of the 3-pass separable Gaussian filter)
resourceSchemas.units: pre-exposed radiance (linear RGB), same space as VolumeTraceRadiance
resourceSchemas.coordinateSpace: 3D froxel grid; each froxel holds a TranslucencyVolumeTracingOctahedronResolution^2 equi-area direction atlas packed into X/Y

transforms.name: texelAddress
transforms.expression: Octahedral atlas texel = uint3(GridCoord.xy*TracingRes + TraceTexelCoord, GridCoord.z); TraceTexelCoord in [0,TracingRes)^2

transforms.name: filter
transforms.expression: separable Gaussian over one axis per pass (SpatialFilterDirection = (1,0,0),(0,1,0),(0,0,1)); 3 passes ping-pong the same RDG name

mathTerms: The filter pass reads VolumeTraceRadiance and VolumeTraceHitDistance and writes this texture; after each pass the C++ variable VolumeTraceRadiance is rebound to the filtered result (LumenTranslucencyVolumeLighting.cpp:886).
Values are quantized with TargetFormatQuantizationError before the R11G11B10 store.
gaps: Three passes use the same RDG name, so a frame contains three filtered textures (the captured 9 variants include repeats); they are not different resources semantically.
The filter is applied to the packed octahedral atlas in 3D, not per-froxel-only; the X/Y neighbourhood crosses texel and froxel boundaries at atlas edges (the shader handles neighbour clamping).

resourceSchemas.quantity: ambient (L0) two-band SH coefficient of the translucency-volume radiance, used by volumetric fog and translucency shading
resourceSchemas.units: linear radiance (L0 coefficient per RGB channel; not pre-exposed, the integrate pass multiplies by View.OneOverPreExposure)
resourceSchemas.coordinateSpace: 3D froxel grid, one texel per froxel

fields.name: AmbientR
fields.decode: red L0 coefficient = Lighting.R.V.x after the PI/res^2 normalization

mathTerms: Lighting is de-preexposed in the integrate pass (VolumeTraceRadiance * View.OneOverPreExposure, LumenTranslucencyVolumeLighting.usf:261) before the SH projection, so this volume is in physical radiance units, unlike VolumeTraceRadiance.
The shader writes a float4(Ambient,0) into a 3-channel R11G11B10 texture: the alpha 0 is discarded by the format and is not stored.
The two-band SH uses basis {1, y, z, x} with signs (0.282095, -0.488603*y, +0.488603*z, -0.488603*x) (SHCommon.ush:221-229).
gaps: The resource is allocated with the pessimistic TranslucencyGIGridResourceSize, which can exceed the logical grid (captured Y=28 vs logical 23); texels outside TranslucencyGIGridSize are not written.
The texture is 3D-tiled (TexCreate_3DTiling); logical texel addressing is decoded here, physical tile/swizzle addressing is RHI/hardware-defined.

resourceSchemas.quantity: directional (L1) two-band SH coefficients of the translucency-volume radiance, luminance-normalized into 3 RGB channels
resourceSchemas.units: three monochrome L1 coefficients (SH V.y, V.z, V.w) scaled by luminance weights; not pre-exposed
resourceSchemas.coordinateSpace: 3D froxel grid, one texel per froxel

fields.name: Directional0
fields.decode: red = dot(Coefficient0, LuminanceWeights) where Coefficient0 = (R.V.y,G.V.y,B.V.y); V.y multiplies -0.488603*dir.y in the SH basis

fields.name: Directional1
fields.decode: green = dot(Coefficient1, LuminanceWeights), Coefficient1 = (R.V.z,G.V.z,B.V.z); V.z multiplies +0.488603*dir.z

fields.name: Directional2
fields.decode: blue = dot(Coefficient2, LuminanceWeights), Coefficient2 = (R.V.w,G.V.w,B.V.w); V.w multiplies -0.488603*dir.x

mathTerms: The compression loses per-channel directionality: only the luminance-weighted direction survives, and the colour ratio is reconstructed from the ambient channel (LumenTranslucencyVolumeShared.ush:61-66).

Component order is SH V.y, V.z, V.w; the two-band basis is V=(0.282095, -0.488603*y, +0.488603*z, -0.488603*x) (SHCommon.ush:221-229), so the three components are ordered (y, z, x) and carry signs. Do not rename them (x,y,z) or drop the signs.
gaps: The stored values are not per-channel SH coefficients; applying them directly as RGB SH (without multiplying by NormalizedAmbientColor) is wrong.
Alpha is explicitly 0 and carries no data.

resourceSchemas.quantity: new history ambient (L0) SH volume produced by temporal reprojection/blending for use next frame
resourceSchemas.units: linear radiance L0 coefficient (not pre-exposed)
resourceSchemas.coordinateSpace: 3D froxel grid, one texel per froxel

fields.name: AmbientR
fields.decode: red L0 of NewHistoryLighting = lerp(Lighting, HistoryLighting, HistoryAlpha)

transforms.name: blend
transforms.expression: NewHistoryLighting = lerp(Lighting, HistoryLighting, HistoryAlpha) when USE_TEMPORAL_REPROJECTION; HistoryAlpha = bNewLightingValid ? HistoryWeight : 1, zeroed when the reprojected UV is outside [0,1)

mathTerms: The new-history ambient is the only part of the SH volume that is quantized with a frame-dependent dither; the directional part is stored raw.
History lighting is decoded from the previous frame's SHLighting0/1 layout before blending.
gaps: The history volume is read via the previous frame's SHLighting0 with a bilinear 3D sample (TranslucencyGIHistory0); the exact previous-frame texture object is not this RDG name, it is the registered external history.

resourceSchemas.quantity: new history directional (L1) SH volume produced by temporal reprojection/blending
resourceSchemas.units: three luminance-weighted L1 coefficients (SH V.y, V.z, V.w); not pre-exposed
resourceSchemas.coordinateSpace: 3D froxel grid, one texel per froxel

transforms.name: encode
transforms.expression: NewHistoryCoefficientL.rgb = lerp(Lighting V, HistoryLighting V, HistoryAlpha); stored = dot(CoefficientL, LuminanceFactors())

transforms.name: decode
transforms.expression: same reconstruction as SHLighting1, applied to the next frame's history sample

mathTerms: Same layout as SHLighting1 but without the frame-dither quantization (written raw, half4).
The history reconstruction uses NormalizedAmbientColor from SHLighting0 of the history frame.
gaps: This is a history-producer buffer: it is consumed through the previous frame's SHLighting0/1 history resources, not by a same-frame pass.

resourceSchemas.quantity: opaque hit distance of each translucency-volume trace direction (or the max trace distance when the ray missed)
resourceSchemas.units: world-space distance (cm) along the cone; no separate hit flag is stored

fields.name: HitDistance
fields.decode: value = min(TraceHitDistance, MaxHalfFloat); TraceHitDistance = MaxTraceDistance when nothing was hit, else TraceResult.OpaqueHitDistance

transforms.name: write
transforms.expression: TraceHitDistance initialized to MaxTraceDistance; set from TraceResult.OpaqueHitDistance when Transparency <= 0.5; stored min(d,MaxHalfFloat)

mathTerms: A miss stores MaxTraceDistance (a large but legal distance), not 0 and not a NaN sentinel; the filter also uses it to weight neighbours.
The cone half-angle / direction for a texel comes from EquiAreaSphericalMapping((TexelCoord+0.5)/TracingRes).
gaps: The value is clamped by R16F storage only; distances above 65504 saturate, so a very large MaxTraceDistance is indistinguishable from a hit at 65504.

resourceSchemas.quantity: incoming radiance traced along each translucency-volume froxel direction
resourceSchemas.units: pre-exposed radiance (multiplied by View.PreExposure; the integrate pass divides by View.OneOverPreExposure)

fields.name: RadianceR
fields.decode: red of the traced radiance, clamped to MaxRayIntensity before storage

transforms.name: store
transforms.expression: TraceRadiance *= View.PreExposure; if max3(TraceRadiance) > MaxRayIntensity, scale down; then QuantizeForFloatRenderTarget

mathTerms: The radiance-cache fallback (when PROBE_SOURCE_MODE_RADIANCE_CACHE) samples the cache and then still multiplies by View.PreExposure (line 154 applies to both sources).
The atlas packs a TracingRes x TracingRes equi-area sphere map into one froxel's X/Y block; the Z coordinate is the froxel slice.
gaps: The max-ray-intensity clamp is applied before the dither quantization, so a clamped texel is not proportional to the true radiance.
The 3D texture is not 3D-tiled for this resource (only the SH volumes use TexCreate_3DTiling), but the RHI may still choose a tiled layout that is not visible in the descriptor flags.
